mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a one‑one (injective) function?

options.A: Every element of the domain maps to a distinct element of the codomain; no two different domain elements have the same image.
options.B: Every element of the codomain is the image of at least one element of the domain.
options.C: Two or more distinct elements of the domain may have the same image in the codomain.
options.D: The function maps the domain onto the entire codomain and also satisfies the condition in option A.

mcqs.answer: Every element of the domain maps to a distinct element of the codomain; no two different domain elements have the same image.
mcqs.explanation: A one‑one (injective) function requires that different inputs produce different outputs, i.e., each element of the domain is associated with a unique element of the codomain. Option B describes onto, C describes many‑one, and D mixes both properties, which is a bijective function, not merely one‑one.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about a many‑one function?

options.A: Each element of the codomain is the image of exactly one element of the domain.
options.B: Two or more distinct elements of the domain may map to the same element of the codomain.
options.C: No two distinct domain elements share the same image.
options.D: Every element of the codomain must be hit by at least one domain element.

mcqs.answer: Two or more distinct elements of the domain may map to the same element of the codomain.
mcqs.explanation: In a many‑one (non‑injective) function, different inputs can produce the same output, which is described by option B. Option A describes a one‑one function, C also describes one‑one, and D describes an onto function.

mcqs.question: An "into" function is best described as:

options.A: A function where every element of the codomain is mapped to by at least one element of the domain.
options.B: A function where some elements of the codomain are never images of any domain element.
options.C: A function that is both one‑one and onto.
options.D: A function that maps each domain element to a unique codomain element and covers the whole codomain.

mcqs.answer: A function where some elements of the codomain are never images of any domain element.
mcqs.explanation: An into function (not onto) does not exhaust the codomain; there exist codomain elements with no pre‑image. Option A describes onto, C describes bijective, and D mixes one‑one with onto, which is bijective.

mcqs.question: Let f : {1,2,3,4} → {a,b,c} be defined by f(1)=a, f(2)=b, f(3)=c, f(4)=c. Which statement is correct?

options.A: f is onto because every element of the codomain {a,b,c} has at least one pre‑image.
options.B: f is not onto because element ‘c’ has two pre‑images.
options.C: f is onto only if the domain and codomain have the same number of elements.
options.D: f cannot be onto because the domain has more elements than the codomain.

mcqs.answer: f is onto because every element of the codomain {a,b,c} has at least one pre‑image.
mcqs.explanation: An onto (surjective) function requires that every codomain element be hit by at least one domain element. Here a, b, and c are all images, so f is onto. The number of pre‑images does not affect surjectivity, so options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following functions is bijective (both one‑one and onto)?
mcqs.explanation: A bijective function must be both injective and surjective. Option B maps each distinct element of the domain to a distinct element of the codomain and covers all codomain elements, satisfying both conditions. Option A is not injective (±x give same value). Option C is injective and onto ℤ, so it is also bijective; however, the codomain is ℤ, and the mapping n→n+1 is onto ℤ, making it bijective as well, but option B is a clearer finite example. Option D is not injective because a and b share the same image.

mcqs.question: A school assigns each student a unique roll number. The function f maps a student to his/her roll number. Which property does this function definitely satisfy?

options.A: It is onto because every roll number is used.
options.B: It is one‑one because no two different students share the same roll number.
options.C: It is into because some roll numbers may be left unused.
options.D: It is many‑one because several students can have the same roll number.

mcqs.answer: It is one‑one because no two different students share the same roll number.
mcqs.explanation: Assigning a unique roll number to each student guarantees that different students have different images, satisfying the definition of a one‑one (injective) function. Whether the function is onto depends on whether every possible roll number is actually assigned, which is not guaranteed, so A and C are not definite. D contradicts the uniqueness condition.

mcqs.question: True or False: Every many‑one function must also be onto.

options.C: True, only when the codomain size is less than the domain size
options.D: False, because many‑one and onto are unrelated properties

mcqs.explanation: A many‑one function merely allows two or more domain elements to share the same image; it does not guarantee that every codomain element is hit. Hence, many‑one does not imply onto. Option D adds an unnecessary statement about unrelatedness; the key point is that the statement is false.

mcqs.question: If a function f : {1,2,3,4,5} → {a,b,c,d} maps 1→a, 2→b, 3→c, 4→c, 5→b, which of the following conclusions is correct?

options.A: f is onto because every element of the codomain appears as an image.
options.B: f is into because element ‘d’ of the codomain has no pre‑image.
options.C: f is one‑one because no two domain elements share the same image.
options.D: f is bijective because it is both one‑one and onto.

mcqs.answer: f is into because element ‘d’ of the codomain has no pre‑image.
mcqs.explanation: An into function fails to cover the entire codomain. Here ‘d’ is never attained, so the function is into (not onto). Option A is wrong because ‘d’ is missing. Option C is wrong because 2 and 5 both map to b, and 3 and 4 both map to c, violating one‑one. Option D is incorrect for the same reasons.
